subject: tourism
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 (with one optional module) · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each).
Section B: very short answers 2 marks (30–50 words), short answers 3 marks (50–80 words), long answers 6 marks (80–120 words).
Section C: attempt either Optional Module I (Travel and Tour Operation Business) or Optional Module II (Hospitality Management) in all its questions.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Tourism helps keep local arts and crafts alive through the sale of souvenirs. (b) Terrorism increases the chance of developing tourism.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it reduces the chance.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) ________ is the foundation of attitude. (b) Societal sustainability can be divided into social and ________.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Bar chart (b) Pie chart. B: (i) Shows proportionate shares of a whole (ii) Compares values of different categories (iii) Shows a trend over time.
State whether True or False. (a) All lines of longitude cut lines of latitude at 90°. (b) Canada has three time zones.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: Canada has six time zones (Australia has three).

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) In 2014 the country from which India received the largest number of foreign tourists was the UK. (b) The share of foreign tourists in India is less than 1% of world tourists.
questions.answer: (a) False: it was the USA. (b) True.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Tourist arrivals means the number of persons who get accommodation at a tourist centre for at least 48 hours. (b) In 2012, America recorded the highest growth in total international tourist arrivals.
questions.answer: (a) False: for at least a night. (b) False: Asia and the Pacific recorded the highest growth (7%).

questions.q: True or False. (a) A virtual team uses computer technology to tie together dispersed members. (b) Heredity alone fixes personality at birth.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name the 7-S mantras of India's tourism policy.
questions.answer: Swagat (welcome), Soochanaa (information), Suvidha (facilitation), Suraksha (security), Sahyog (cooperation), Sanrachnaa (infrastructure) and Safai (cleanliness).

questions.q: Explain the relationship between transportation and tourism in two points.
questions.answer: Transport links the tourist-generating area with the destination, so tourism is impossible without it. Its capacity, speed, comfort and safety decide the pace of tourist flow.

questions.q: Write any two features of the Santoor.
questions.answer: It is a trapezoid-shaped folk instrument of Kashmir made of walnut wood with many strings. It is played with two light hammers (mezrab) and is used in Sufiana kalam.

questions.q: Name the two Buddhist architectural forms and state their use.
questions.answer: A stupa is a mound built over Buddha's relics and at sites of his life events. A vihara is a monastery and a chaitya is a congregational hall for preaching and teaching.

questions.q: What is Rath Yatra? Where is it held?
questions.answer: It is the annual festival at Puri when the idols of Jagannath, Balram and Subhadra are taken in raths to the Gundicha temple and brought back after some days.

questions.q: Who was Begum Samru? Why is Sardhana famous?
questions.answer: Begum Samru was the Roman Catholic wife of a German mercenary, who commanded his force after his death. She built the beautiful Sardhana church near Meerut, a heritage site visited in March and November.

questions.q: Give two reasons for the growth of domestic tourism in India.
questions.answer: Rising income levels and purchasing power have grown. The emergence of a dynamic middle class has pushed domestic travel.

questions.q: Name any three of the top ten tourist destinations of the world in 2015.
questions.answer: France, the United States and Spain (then Italy, the United Kingdom, China, Poland, Mexico, Canada and Hungary).

questions.q: Explain 'coherence' as a principle of effective writing.
questions.answer: Coherence means relation and clarity among the parts of the writing. It applies to sentences, paragraphs and the whole message.

questions.q: Who are the intermediaries in the marketing environment?
questions.answer: They are wholesalers, retailers and agents who help bring the product to the consumer and create place and time utility.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three positive economic impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: (i) It earns foreign exchange and helps the balance of trade. (ii) The government earns revenue through taxes, entry fees and import duty. (iii) It creates jobs, including informal ones, and encourages investment in infrastructure.

questions.q: What are special or thematic maps? Explain any two thematic maps.
questions.answer: Special or thematic maps give information on a theme such as climate or roads. (i) A railway map shows gauge, route length, electrified or diesel sections and single or double track, helping tourists plan train journeys. (ii) A road map shows national and state highways, petrol pumps, lodging and the distance matrix.

questions.q: Explain the role of a tourist transport system in three points.
questions.answer: (i) It links tourist-generating areas with destinations. (ii) The capacity of the transport system decides the pace of tourist flow. (iii) Comfort, speed, safety, discounts and refreshments act as incentives and good or bad experiences stay in the tourist's mind.

questions.q: Distinguish between advertising and sales promotion (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Advertising is impersonal; sales promotion is personal. (ii) Advertising aims at creating demand; sales promotion aims at increasing sales. (iii) Advertising reaches a huge audience but gives no immediate feedback; sales promotion has limited scope and gives immediate feedback.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the process of communication and the barriers to it, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) The sender has a message. (ii) Encoding turns it into symbols. (iii) The channel carries it to the receiver. (iv) The receiver decodes it. (v) Feedback completes the process. (vi) Barriers are noise, distance, information overload, language and an unfamiliar medium.

questions.q: Explain the functions of marketing with reference to tourism, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Market research: systematic investigation to know tourists' needs. (ii) Product planning and development: designing and improving products such as tour packages. (iii) Segmentation: grouping tourists by needs, e.g. religious tourists. (iv) Promotion: informing and persuading through advertising, publicity, personal selling and sales promotion. (v) Selling: direct, retail, agency, tele-sales and online. (vi) The marketing mix of the four Ps plus people, physical evidence and process guides these functions.

sections.title: Optional Module I (Travel and Tour Operation Business): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why is corporate social responsibility important? Explain in three points.
questions.answer: (i) Business should make a direct positive contribution to society. (ii) It supports training, basic amenities in government schools and empowerment of women. (iii) Destination sustainability is possible only when all stakeholders take social responsibility.

questions.q: Distinguish between GIT and FIT itineraries (three points).
questions.answer: (i) GIT follows a fixed itinerary; FIT is flexible. (ii) GIT is cheaper through bulk buying; FIT costs more for the flexibility. (iii) GIT groups share a common affiliation; FIT suits independent travellers who want personal choices.

sections.title: Optional Module II (Hospitality Management): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps of an individual reservation procedure (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Receive the request and ask for dates and room type. (ii) Match with room availability on the computerised system and offer alternatives if needed. (iii) Record the guest details and give a confirmation number.

questions.q: Explain any three security measures taken by a hotel.
questions.answer: (i) Limit access points and monitor them with CCTV. (ii) Scan guest baggage and hotel supplies. (iii) Guest profiling, employee verification and key control.
